job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many people often assume that the Prime Minister is the supreme head of the country, but in our parliamentary democracy, the President holds that position as the formal head of state. While the Prime Minister exercises real executive powers, they must remain accountable to the legislature. A common confusion also exists regarding the hierarchy of our legislative houses. Because the Rajya Sabha is called the 'Upper House,' some believe it holds more power than the Lok Sabha. In reality, the Lok Sabha is far more powerful because its members are directly elected by the people, and it has the final say in financial matters and no-confidence motions. Furthermore, the daily administration of government policy is carried out by the permanent executive, consisting of civil servants. While these officers are highly skilled and provide essential expertise, they do not make the final political decisions. Instead, the political executive, which includes the ministers elected by citizens, takes the ultimate responsibility for policy choices. This structure ensures that the government remains responsive to the public will rather than being controlled by unelected officials. By separating the roles of the political and permanent executive, and balancing the powers between the two houses of Parliament, our constitution maintains a system of checks and balances that protects the democratic process.
response.summary: The President is the formal head of state, while the Lok Sabha holds more power than the Rajya Sabha. Final policy decisions are made by elected ministers, not by civil servants.
